items.note: Untap, upkeep, and draw. You ready your board, resolve beginning-of-turn triggers, then draw for turn.
Play a land (if available), cast spells, and activate abilities before combat.
Beginning of combat, declare attackers, declare blockers, combat damage, and end of combat.
A second main phase for post-combat plays, using any remaining mana and resources.
End step and cleanup. End-step triggers resolve, then you discard to hand size and remove marked damage.

items.label: Explore
items.title: Explore
items.description: Reveal the top card of your library. If it's a land card, put it into your hand. Otherwise put a +1/+1 counter on this creature, then you may put the revealed card into your graveyard.

items.label: Scry
items.title: Scry
items.description: Look at the top x cards of your library, then put any number of them on the bottom and the rest back on top in any order.

items.label: Surveil
items.title: Surveil
items.description: Look at the top x cards of your library, then put any number of them into your graveyard and the rest back on top in any order.

items.label: Annihilator
items.title: Annihilator
items.description: Whenever a creature with annihilator N attacks, the defending player sacrifices N permanents.
bullets: Annihilator triggers when the attack is declared, before blockers are chosen, so the defending player sacrifices before they can block.
The defending player chooses which permanents to sacrifice — they can choose lands, creatures, or anything else.
Multiple instances of annihilator add up — a creature with annihilator 2 attacking alongside another with annihilator 1 forces three sacrifices.
Even if the creature is removed from combat after the trigger is placed on the stack, the trigger still resolves.

items.label: Changeling
items.title: Changeling
items.description: This card is every creature type at all times.
bullets: Changeling applies in all zones — in hand, library, graveyard, and exile, not just on the battlefield.
A changeling creature benefits from all tribal effects, such as lord bonuses, regardless of the specific creature type mentioned.
If an effect counts creature types, changeling creatures count as one creature of every type simultaneously.
Changeling overrides any 'this creature is only [type]' restrictions — it is always all types.

items.label: Copy
items.title: Copy
items.description: Copies replicate an existing permanent or spell exactly, including its characteristics and abilities.
bullets: Copies do not copy the original's counters, attachments, or temporary effects unless stated.
Some copy effects create tokens, while others do not; follow the exact card text.
If copying a creature, the copy uses the copiable values of the chosen object.
If you copy a permanent that's a copy of something else, you copy the current state of the first copy.

items.label: Deathtouch
items.title: Deathtouch
items.description: A creature with deathtouch destroys any creature it deals any amount of damage to.
bullets: Any nonzero amount of damage from a source with deathtouch is considered lethal, whether it's combat damage or noncombat damage.
Deathtouch interacts powerfully with trample — because any 1 damage is lethal, all remaining damage tramples over.
Multiple instances of deathtouch are redundant.

items.label: Defender
items.title: Defender
items.description: A creature with defender can't attack.
bullets: Defender doesn't prevent the creature from blocking - it's purely an attack restriction.
Creatures with defender can still use abilities that cost tapping.
If a creature loses defender via an effect, it can attack normally.

items.label: Dethrone
items.title: Dethrone
items.description: Whenever a creature with dethrone attacks the player with the most life (or tied for the most), put a +1/+1 counter on it.
bullets: Dethrone checks life totals at the time the creature attacks, not when damage is dealt.
In a tie for the most life, attacking any of the tied players triggers dethrone.
Dethrone was introduced in Commander 2014 and is designed for multiplayer games.
The +1/+1 counter is placed regardless of whether the attack connects or deals damage.

items.label: Double Strike
items.title: Double Strike
items.description: A creature with double strike deals combat damage in both the first strike and normal combat damage steps.
bullets: The creature effectively hits twice - once during first strike damage and once during regular damage.
Double strike includes first strike; the creature does not get a third hit.
If blocked by a creature that dies in the first strike step, the double striker still deals its second instance of damage to the player if it has trample.

items.label: Exalted
items.title: Exalted
items.description: Whenever a creature attacks alone, each creature you control with exalted gives the attacker +1/+1 until end of turn.
bullets: All exalted triggers stack — if you control three creatures with exalted and one attacks alone, it gets +3/+3 until end of turn.
'Attacks alone' means it is the only creature declared as an attacker during that combat.
The bonus applies even if the exalted creature itself is not the attacker.
Exalted triggers before blockers are declared, so the bonus is already applied when damage is calculated.

items.label: First Strike
items.title: First Strike
items.description: A creature with first strike deals combat damage before creatures without first strike.
bullets: Combat damage is dealt in two steps: first strikers deal damage, then everyone else does.
If a first striker kills its blocker, the blocker deals no combat damage back.
Granting first strike after the first strike damage step doesn't retroactively deal damage.

items.label: Flying
items.title: Flying
items.description: A creature with flying can't be blocked except by creatures with flying or reach.
bullets: Flying is an evasion ability that restricts blocking.
Creatures without flying or reach cannot block a creature with flying.
Multiple instances of flying are redundant.

items.label: Forestwalk
items.title: Forestwalk
items.description: A creature with forestwalk can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Forest.
bullets: Forestwalk checks only whether the defending player controls at least one Forest.
If the condition is true, no creatures can block it, regardless of their abilities.
Landwalk is an evasion ability and does not affect attacking requirements.

items.label: Goad
items.title: Goad
items.description: A goaded creature attacks each combat if able, and attacks a player other than the goader if able.
bullets: Goaded creatures must attack - they can't choose to stay back.
If the goaded creature can't attack the goading player due to a restriction, it attacks another player or a planeswalker.
If goaded by multiple players, the creature avoids all of them if able.
Goad lasts until your next turn.

items.label: Haste
items.title: Haste
items.description: A creature with haste can attack and tap on the turn it enters the battlefield.
bullets: Normally, creatures can't attack or use tap abilities the turn they come under your control, also known as summoning sickness.
Haste only affects the can't attack/tap restriction - it doesn't prevent other restrictions.
Losing haste after attacking doesn't remove the creature from combat.

items.label: Indestructible
items.title: Indestructible
items.description: A permanent with indestructible can't be destroyed.
bullets: Effects that say destroy don't affect indestructible permanents.
Lethal damage and damage from a source with deathtouch don't destroy indestructible creatures, but the damage stays marked on them.
Sacrificing or exiling an indestructible permanent still works - those aren't destruction.

items.label: Infect
items.title: Infect
items.description: A creature with infect deals damage to players as poison counters and to creatures as -1/-1 counters instead of regular damage.
bullets: A player who accumulates ten or more poison counters loses the game, regardless of life total.
Infect damage does not reduce a player's life total — it only gives poison counters.
Damage from infect sources to creatures adds -1/-1 counters rather than marking damage, so toughness reductions are permanent until the creature leaves the battlefield.
Combining infect with effects that pump power quickly closes out games through the poison win condition.
Wither is a similar ability that also deals damage as -1/-1 counters to creatures, but does not give poison counters to players.

items.label: Lifelink
items.title: Lifelink
items.description: Whenever a creature with lifelink deals damage, its controller gains that much life.
bullets: Lifelink works with combat damage and noncombat damage, as long as the source is the one with lifelink.
The life gain happens when the damage is dealt, not when the creature is later removed from battle.
Multiple instances of lifelink are redundant and do not increase the amount of life gained.
If a 5/5 creature with lifelink deals damage, its controller gains 5 life no matter the amount of defense the blocker has.

items.label: Lore Counter
items.title: Lore Counters
items.description: Sagas use lore counters to track chapters. A Saga enters with a lore counter, and its controller adds one at the beginning of their precombat main phase.
bullets: Chapter abilities trigger based on the number of lore counters - Chapter I triggers on the first, Chapter II on the second, and so on.
Once the final chapter resolves, the Saga is sacrificed as a state-based action.
Lore counters can be added or removed by other card effects to speed up or reset Sagas.

items.label: Magecraft
items.title: Magecraft
items.description: Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, each ability with magecraft triggers.
bullets: Magecraft triggers on both casting and copying — copying a spell without casting it still counts.
Multiple magecraft abilities on different permanents all trigger from the same spell cast.
Cheap cantrips and rituals are especially effective for triggering magecraft repeatedly in one turn.
Magecraft was introduced in Strixhaven and is the signature mechanic of its spellcasting-themed sets.

items.label: Menace
items.title: Menace
items.description: A creature with menace can't be blocked except by two or more creatures.
bullets: One blocker is not enough - at least two creatures must block it.
If one of the two blockers is removed before damage, the block is still legal and the creature remains blocked.
Multiple instances of menace are redundant - it still only needs two blockers.

items.label: Myriad
items.title: Myriad
items.description: Whenever a creature with myriad attacks, for each other opponent, create a token copy of it tapped and attacking that opponent or a planeswalker they control.
bullets: Tokens created by myriad are exiled at the end of combat, regardless of what happened to them.
Myriad is designed for Commander — it lets one creature effectively attack all opponents simultaneously.
Triggers and abilities on the tokens (including on-attack triggers) still resolve even though the tokens are later exiled.
The original creature attacks one player or planeswalker; the tokens each attack a different opponent.

items.label: Planeswalk
items.title: Planeswalk
items.description: A creature with planeswalk can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Plane card.
bullets: Planeswalk follows the same pattern as landwalk abilities, but checks for Plane cards.
If the defending player controls a Plane, the creature is unblockable for that combat.
This ability is uncommon and mostly appears in Planechase-related designs.

items.label: Prowess
items.title: Prowess
items.description: Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
bullets: Prowess triggers each time a noncreature spell is cast, so casting multiple spells in one turn gives multiple bonuses.
Artifacts, enchantments, planeswalkers, and instants or sorceries all trigger prowess.
Multiple instances of prowess each trigger separately, giving +1/+1 per instance per spell cast.
The bonus lasts only until end of turn and doesn't carry over to subsequent turns.

items.label: Reach
items.title: Reach
items.description: A creature with reach can block creatures with flying.
bullets: Reach allows a creature to block attackers with flying that it otherwise couldn't.
Reach does not grant flying - the creature still can't be used to satisfy flying requirements.
Multiple instances of reach are redundant.

items.label: Summoning Sickness
items.title: Summoning Sickness
items.description: A creature can't attack or use tap abilities the turn it comes under your control, unless it has haste.
bullets: Summoning sickness is not a keyword ability - it's a game rule that applies to all creatures.
It only affects attacking and abilities with the tap symbol - untap abilities and non-tap activated abilities work fine.
A creature that has been under your control since the beginning of your most recent turn is no longer sick.
Gaining control of an opponent's creature gives it summoning sickness unless it has haste.

items.label: Swampwalk
items.title: Swampwalk
items.description: A creature with swampwalk can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Swamp.
bullets: Swampwalk checks only whether the defending player controls at least one Swamp.
If the condition is true, no creatures can block it, regardless of their abilities.
Like other landwalk abilities, swampwalk only matters while attacking.

items.label: Toxic
items.title: Toxic
items.description: Whenever a creature with toxic N deals combat damage to a player, that player gets N poison counters in addition to the normal damage.
bullets: Unlike infect, toxic damage still reduces the player's life total — the poison counters are additional.
Multiple instances of toxic stack — a creature with toxic 1 and a separate toxic 2 ability gives 3 poison counters per combat hit.
A player with ten or more poison counters loses the game, regardless of their life total.
Toxic only applies to combat damage, not noncombat damage from that creature.

items.label: Trample
items.title: Trample
items.description: Excess combat damage dealt by a creature with trample to a blocking creature carries over to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.
bullets: You must assign at least lethal damage to all blockers before assigning leftover damage to the player or planeswalker.
If no creatures block, all damage goes to the player or planeswalker.
Trample works with deathtouch - any nonzero damage is considered lethal, so the rest tramples over.

items.label: Vigilance
items.title: Vigilance
items.description: Attacking doesn't cause a creature with vigilance to tap.
bullets: The creature still declares an attack as normal - it just doesn't tap when doing so.
This means it can both attack and block on subsequent turns without needing to untap.
Vigilance only applies to attacking, not to other tap-based abilities.

items.label: Hexproof
items.title: Hexproof
items.description: A permanent with hexproof can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control.
bullets: Only opponent spells and abilities are affected — you can still target your own hexproof permanents.
Non-targeting effects like board wipes still affect hexproof creatures.

You can't cast an Aura spell targeting a hexproof creature. However, effects that put an Aura onto the battlefield without casting it (such as 'search your library for an Aura and attach it') bypass hexproof since no targeting occurs.

items.label: Hexproof (Black)
items.title: Hexproof from Black
items.description: This permanent can't be the target of black spells or abilities your opponents control.
bullets: Hexproof from black only blocks targeting — non-targeting black effects such as 'destroy all creatures' still affect it.
You can still target your own permanent with black spells or abilities.
It does not prevent black creatures from blocking, or black Auras from attaching through non-casting effects.
Multiple hexproof-from-[color] abilities are redundant — one instance is sufficient.

items.label: Hexproof (Blue)
items.title: Hexproof from Blue
items.description: This permanent can't be the target of blue spells or abilities your opponents control.
bullets: Hexproof from blue only blocks targeting — non-targeting blue effects such as 'destroy all creatures' still affect it.
You can still target your own permanent with blue spells or abilities.
It does not prevent blue creatures from blocking, or blue Auras from attaching through non-casting effects.
Multiple hexproof-from-[color] abilities are redundant — one instance is sufficient.

items.label: Hexproof (Green)
items.title: Hexproof from Green
items.description: This permanent can't be the target of green spells or abilities your opponents control.
bullets: Hexproof from green only blocks targeting — non-targeting green effects such as 'destroy all creatures' still affect it.
You can still target your own permanent with green spells or abilities.
It does not prevent green creatures from blocking, or green Auras from attaching through non-casting effects.
Multiple hexproof-from-[color] abilities are redundant — one instance is sufficient.

items.label: Hexproof (Red)
items.title: Hexproof from Red
items.description: This permanent can't be the target of red spells or abilities your opponents control.
bullets: Hexproof from red only blocks targeting — non-targeting red effects such as 'destroy all creatures' still affect it.
You can still target your own permanent with red spells or abilities.
It does not prevent red creatures from blocking, or red Auras from attaching through non-casting effects.
Multiple hexproof-from-[color] abilities are redundant — one instance is sufficient.

items.label: Hexproof (White)
items.title: Hexproof from White
items.description: This permanent can't be the target of white spells or abilities your opponents control.
bullets: Hexproof from white only blocks targeting — non-targeting white effects such as 'destroy all creatures' still affect it.
You can still target your own permanent with white spells or abilities.
It does not prevent white creatures from blocking, or white Auras from attaching through non-casting effects.
Multiple hexproof-from-[color] abilities are redundant — one instance is sufficient.

items.label: Poison
items.title: Poison Counter
items.description: A player who has ten or more poison counters loses the game.
bullets: Poison counters are given to players, not creatures.
Creatures with toxic or toxic X deal X poison counters in addition to normal combat damage.
Poison counters persist - there's no natural way to remove them outside of specific card effects.
Infect damage gives poison counters equal to the damage dealt instead of regular damage.

items.label: Ward
items.title: Ward
items.description: Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter it unless that player pays the ward cost.
bullets: Ward triggers when any opponent's spell or ability targets the permanent — not just removal spells.
If the opponent doesn't pay the ward cost, the targeting spell or ability is countered entirely.
Ward only protects from opponents' effects — you can freely target your own permanents with ward.
Multiple ward triggers on the same permanent must each be paid separately if triggered at the same time.
Ward doesn't prevent non-targeting effects such as board wipes that say 'destroy all creatures.'

items.label: Can't Attack
items.title: Can't Attack
items.description: The creature is unable to declare an attack.
bullets: This can be caused by abilities like defender, or by external effects that prohibit attacking.
If the restriction is removed, for example if defender is stripped, the creature can attack normally.
Effects that force a creature to attack won't override a can't attack restriction - restrictions win over requirements.

items.label: Can't Block
items.title: Can't Block
items.description: The creature is unable to declare a block.
bullets: This is typically imposed by another creature's ability, for example creatures your opponents control can't block.
If the effect ends before the declare blockers step, the creature can block normally.
Like with attacking, can't block restrictions override effects that would force a creature to block.

items.label: Finality
items.title: Finality
items.description: If a permanent with finality would be put into a graveyard from the battlefield, exile it instead.
bullets: This is a replacement effect, not a trigger - it modifies where the permanent goes.
Finality prevents reanimation strategies - the card can't be brought back from the graveyard because it never gets there.
If the permanent is a token, it can be exiled, then it ceases to exist as a state-based action.

items.label: Phase Out
items.title: Phase Out
items.description: A phased-out permanent is treated as though it doesn't exist until it phases in.
bullets: Phasing doesn't cause a permanent to leave or enter the battlefield.
Auras, Equipment, and counters attached to that permanent phase out with it and return with it.
Triggers for leaving or entering the battlefield do not happen from phasing.

items.label: Shield Counter
items.title: Shield Counter
items.description: If a permanent with a shield counter would be dealt damage or destroyed, remove a shield counter from it instead.
bullets: A shield counter protects that permanent from one destruction event or one damage event.
When this happens, one shield counter is removed instead of that event occurring.
Multiple shield counters protect the permanent multiple times.
Shield counters are physical counters placed on the permanent; they can be added or removed by various card effects.
This differs from ward - ward counters an opponent's spell or ability targeting the permanent, while shield protects from damage and destruction effects.

items.label: Cascade
items.title: Cascade
items.description: When you cast a spell with cascade, you exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a card with a lower mana value than the spell.
bullets: You may cast the exiled card without paying its mana cost.
Any cards exiled this way (that weren't cast) are put under your library in a random order after the spell resolves, unless an effect changes that.
Cascade only applies when the spell is cast, not when it is later copied or replayed.

items.label: Convoke
items.title: Convoke
items.description: Your creatures can help cast this spell. Each creature you tap as you cast this spell pays for {1} or one mana of that creature's color.
bullets: Tapping a creature for convoke is part of paying the spell's cost — it happens during casting, not as a separate action.
Creatures affected by summoning sickness can still be tapped for convoke, since it's a cost payment rather than an activated ability.
You can tap as many untapped creatures as you have, but only up to what the spell actually costs.
Convoke reduces the mana you need to pay but cannot reduce the cost below zero.

items.label: Crew
items.title: Crew
items.description: Crew is an activated ability of Vehicles. You tap untapped creatures you control with total power N or more to pay the crew cost.
bullets: You must pay the crew cost with untapped creatures you control.
Only creatures that are untapped and controlled by you can be used to pay the cost.
Once a vehicle is crewed, it can attack and block as a creature for the turn's duration.

items.label: Echo
items.title: Echo
items.description: Echo means that at the beginning of your upkeep, if this permanent came under your control since the beginning of your last upkeep, you sacrifice it unless you pay its echo cost.
bullets: Echo checks at your upkeep, not while casting the spell.
If you don't pay, you sacrifice that permanent.
Echo applies once per permanent entering under your control in that window.

items.label: Emerge
items.title: Emerge
items.description: You may cast a spell with emerge by sacrificing a creature and paying the emerge cost reduced by the sacrificed creature's mana value.
bullets: The sacrificed creature's mana value reduces the emerge cost — sacrificing a higher-cost creature makes the emerge spell cheaper.
The sacrifice is part of paying the cost and happens as you cast the spell, not after it resolves.
Death triggers and sacrifice synergies from the sacrificed creature still resolve after the emerge spell resolves.
You may still pay the full mana cost of the emerge card rather than using emerge.

items.label: Encore
items.title: Encore
items.description: Pay the encore cost and exile this card from your graveyard: For each opponent, create a token copy of this card that attacks them this turn if able. Those tokens have haste and are sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step. Activate only as a sorcery.
bullets: Encore is activated from the graveyard — it is not cast, so it can't be countered as a spell.
Each token attacks a different opponent, making encore especially powerful in Commander with multiple opponents.
Tokens are sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step, even if they didn't attack.
Since the original card is exiled to activate encore, it can't be reanimated from the graveyard afterward.
Encore can only be activated as a sorcery — at the start of your main phase with an empty stack.

items.label: Fabricate
items.title: Fabricate
items.description: When a permanent with fabricate N enters the battlefield, put N +1/+1 counters on it or create N 1/1 colorless Servo artifact creature tokens.
bullets: You choose one option — counters or Servo tokens — you can't split between the two.
The choice is made when the ability resolves, after the permanent has already entered the battlefield.
Servo tokens are 1/1 colorless artifact creatures with no abilities.
Fabricate 2 gives either two +1/+1 counters on the permanent or two Servo tokens.

items.label: Flash
items.title: Flash
items.description: A spell with flash can be cast at any time you could cast an instant.
bullets: Flash lets you play cards during your opponent's turn.
This is commonly used to surprise opponents with instant-speed interaction or threats.

items.label: Flashback
items.title: Flashback
items.description: Flashback lets you cast a card from your graveyard for its flashback cost.
bullets: The card must be in your graveyard to use flashback.
You still pay the listed flashback cost when casting it this way.
If a spell cast with flashback would leave the stack, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else.

items.label: Foretell
items.title: Foretell
items.description: During your turn, you may pay {2} and exile a card with foretell from your hand face down. On a later turn, you may cast it from exile for its foretell cost.
bullets: When you foretell a card, you exile it face down as a separate game object and retain knowledge of what it is.
On a later turn, you can cast the foretold card from exile by paying its foretell cost instead of its normal mana cost.
The foretell cost is typically lower than the card's normal mana cost, allowing you to play cards ahead of tempo.
You can take the foretell special action only once each turn.
Forgetting about a foretold card, for example losing track of which turn it was foretold, doesn't prevent you from casting it later.

items.label: Kicker
items.title: Kicker
items.description: Kicker lets you pay an additional cost as you cast a spell to get a bonus effect.
bullets: The kicker cost is chosen by the card and is paid when the spell is cast.
If you pay it, the spell gains an extra effect printed on the card.
Different cards use kicker for different bonuses, so the exact effect depends on the card.

items.label: Mutate
items.title: Mutate
items.description: Mutate lets you cast a creature spell for its mutate cost targeting a non-Human creature you own. If it resolves, the cards merge into one creature.
bullets: You choose whether the new card goes on top or underneath.
The merged creature has the characteristics of the top card and abilities from all cards in the pile.
If the merged creature leaves the battlefield, each card goes to the appropriate zone individually.

items.label: Ninjutsu
items.title: Ninjutsu
items.description: Pay the ninjutsu cost and return an unblocked attacker you control to your hand: Put this card onto the battlefield from your hand tapped and attacking.
bullets: Ninjutsu can only be activated after blockers are declared and the target creature is confirmed to be unblocked.
The deployed ninja is already attacking and deals combat damage normally, including triggering any on-attack or on-damage abilities.
Summoning sickness doesn't apply to the ninja since it entered already attacking — not via a normal declare attackers step.
The swapped-out creature returns to your hand and can be recast on a later turn.

items.label: Partner
items.title: Partner
items.description: Two legendary creatures with partner can both be your commanders at the same time.
bullets: Each partner starts in the command zone and can be cast independently at any time you could normally cast your commander.
Commander tax applies to each partner separately — casting one only increases that creature's future cost.
'Partner with [name]' is a variant that only pairs with one specific named card, not any other partner creature.
Having two commanders expands the color identity available for deckbuilding.
If one partner is moved to the command zone, the other can remain on the battlefield as normal.

items.label: Persist
items.title: Persist
items.description: When a creature with persist dies, if it had no -1/-1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a -1/-1 counter on it.
bullets: Persist only triggers if the creature had no -1/-1 counters at the time it died.
If a creature has both persist and undying, dying with no counters triggers both; the first to resolve adds a counter, preventing the second from returning it.
Removing the -1/-1 counter (for example with a proliferate reversal or counter removal) resets persist, allowing it to trigger again.
Persist is popular in Commander with sacrifice synergies since it repeatedly returns the creature to generate death triggers.

items.label: Protection
items.title: Protection
items.description: A permanent with protection from a quality can't be Damaged, Enchanted/Equipped, Blocked, or Targeted by things of that quality — remember the acronym D.E.B.T.
bullets: Damage from sources with that quality is prevented.
Enchantments or Equipment with that quality can't be attached to the protected permanent and fall off if they somehow end up attached.
Creatures with that quality can't block the protected creature.
The protected permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities from sources with that quality.
Protection doesn't prevent non-targeting effects — board wipes that say 'destroy all creatures' still destroy it unless they specifically target.

items.label: Storm
items.title: Storm
items.description: When you cast a spell with storm, copy it for each spell cast before it this turn. You may choose new targets for each copy.
bullets: Copies resolve one by one from the top of the stack — the last copy created resolves first.
The copies are placed on the stack but are not cast, so they can't trigger storm again or be countered by spells that target spells on the stack.
Storm counts all spells cast this turn by any player, not just you.
In Commander, storm can be a game-ending combo when many spells have already been cast in one turn.

items.label: Undying
items.title: Undying
items.description: When a creature with undying dies, if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a +1/+1 counter on it.
bullets: Undying only triggers if the creature had no +1/+1 counters at the time it died.
If a creature has both undying and persist, dying with no counters triggers both; the first to resolve adds a counter, preventing the second from returning it.
Removing the +1/+1 counter resets undying, allowing it to trigger again if the creature dies.
Undying pairs well with sacrifice outlets in Commander for repeated death triggers and enters-the-battlefield effects.

items.label: Unearth
items.title: Unearth
items.description: Pay the unearth cost: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield. It gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step or if it would leave the battlefield. Activate only as a sorcery.
bullets: Unearth returns the creature temporarily — it has haste and is useful for one-turn burst of value or damage.
If the creature would leave the battlefield for any reason before the end step (bounced, destroyed, exiled), it's exiled instead of going to any other zone.
Since the card is exiled after unearth, it cannot be reanimated again from the graveyard.
Unearth can only be activated as a sorcery — during your main phase with an empty stack.

items.label: Airbend
items.title: Airbend
items.description: Exile target permanent or spell. While it's exiled this way, its owner may cast it for {2} rather than its mana cost.
bullets: Only the {2} alternative cost applies — other alternate costs don't work and X is always 0.
Lands exiled this way can't be played from exile since lands may only be played from hand.
Tokens cease to exist when exiled and can't be returned.
The timing of casting from exile follows the card's normal restrictions unless otherwise stated.

items.label: Earthbend
items.title: Earthbend
items.description: Target land you control becomes a 0/0 creature with haste that's still a land. Put X +1/+1 counters on it. When it dies or is exiled as a creature, return it to the battlefield tapped.
bullets: The animated land is still a land — it still produces mana and counts toward your land total.
The +1/+1 counters remain on the land even after it stops being a creature.
Multiple earthbend effects can stack additional counters onto the same land.
If the land dies or is exiled while animated, it returns to the battlefield tapped, triggering any relevant enters-the-battlefield effects.

items.label: Firebend
items.title: Firebend
items.description: When a creature with firebend N attacks, add N red mana. That mana can only be used during the combat phase and is lost at the end of combat.
bullets: The red mana is available from when the attack trigger resolves through the end of combat.
Unused mana from firebend is lost when the combat phase ends — it doesn't carry over to later phases.
Best used with instants or activated abilities that can be triggered during combat.
Multiple creatures with firebend attacking simultaneously each add their mana separately.

items.label: Waterbend
items.title: Waterbend
items.description: When paying a waterbend cost, you may tap untapped artifacts or creatures you control to pay for each generic mana in that cost rather than paying mana.
bullets: Only generic mana in the cost can be paid this way — colored mana requirements must still be paid normally.
Tapping a permanent for waterbend doesn't require that permanent to produce mana on its own.
Similar to convoke and improvise, but applies to abilities and additional costs, not just spell casting.
Creatures with vigilance are especially effective since they can attack and still be tapped for waterbend costs.
